title: How do you monitor the de of a hologram

posts.topic_title: How do you monitor the de of a hologram
posts.author: JohnFP
posts.post_subject: How do you monitor the de of a hologram
posts.content_md:
How do you monitor the de of a hologram as it develops in the tray?

Well, this may sound simplistic.

But use a tray that is made of glass. Mount an LED that is of wavelength that your film is not sesitive to underneath the glass tray. Make a fixtur that mounts a photo diode above the tray which is lined up with the LED and has a meter attached to it. The hologram is placed in the tray and lays between the LED and the photodiode. As is darkens it starts to block the light which is measured on the meter. You would need to calibrate the DE with the readings on the meter.

![Image](http://www.sketchys.com/Holograms/HoloStuff/Drawings/DEMeter.jpg)

posts.content_md: I am guessing you mean measuring the Density and not the DE (defraction efficiency). To measure the defraction efficiency you can take a developed and bleached hologram and see how much light blocks while reconstructing.

posts.topic_title: How do you monitor the de of a hologram
posts.author: Gary Deal
posts.post_subject: How do you monitor the de of a hologram
posts.content_md:
Let's see, to measure the diffraction efficiency of a hologram in the developer, I'd think you'd first have to figure out what wavelength the wet hologram would diffract while wet, then supply the wavelength in a more or less linear form through the hologram, then measure the diffracted and undiffracted light(?) and compare the two. That question mark is because what the hologram would diffract while it was wet would be probably be outside the visible spectrum.

Dinesh, that calculating fiend, says he's got a method that worked. Properly placed IR diodes and a good power meter?

 I made a "wet" hologram a while back. I soaked the film in developer, clamped it between two glass plates, exposed it and watched. The film darkened a bit and I gave it some extra exposure, I then put it back in the developer (Kodak HRP 1:2) to finish developing. After the usual process I pulled it from the wash and took a look. Wet, the image showed. As it dried, I watched it change color and disappear as it passed beyond the visible spectrum. Once the image was gone I could bring it back by breathing on it, or better by re-wetting it, but I found limited novelty in an invisible hologram.

 There may be practical uses for this in humidity (or water content) indicators, or for holograms that bees can see while we can't.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.post_subject: How do you monitor the de of a hologram
posts.content_md:
Gary, I too was playing with the idea in my head about putting the set up during the bleaching bath but realized until the hologram is dried the swelled emulsion in a phase hologram is not really that phased (?lol). But as Colin stated as a post measurement this system could be used to determing the DE, I believe. What I was shooting for through the density configuration is to be able to monitor the density, real time, so that one could control that parameter and get more consistant results. This would be nicely applicable to transmission holograms. Although crude this system would give you a density but one can get density without even getting a hologram.

Now back to the DE question.

What is an actual physical property of the hologram as it is being developed? What about when it moves from anamplitude to a phase hologram or from an amplitude to a reversal hologram in the bleach process? Can an array of diodes be incorporeated such that the diffration can be seen to move from the straight to a close angle of the reference beam? How about a Diode that moves perpendicular to the plate above the processing solution to see efficiencies formed at the object depth? What is the replay wavelength of a hologram shot at 633 but still wet in the developing bath? This would be some fun research.
